ledger.claim: The fare breakdown charges SGD 2.00 for the 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry', but this trip's own GPS trace never goes near that gantry. The derived gantry-proximity analysis puts the closest fix to the gantry's coordinates at 4,851.46 m away, and records that no gap in the trace brackets a closest approach to it. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to a trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing; at roughly nineteen times that radius, not a single one of the 107 fixes is a crossing. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refunded in full as a standalone correction.

The rider does not need to win a route-deviation finding to recover this line: POL-RD-09(4) makes the billing-integrity correction available whether or not a deviation exists. The record in fact shows the deviation is NOT established, and the rider does not pretend otherwise - the derived figures give an excess of 0.65 km and 5.04%, and POL-RD-01 requires an excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% before a deviation exists. Both tests fail, so no POL-RD-02 distance refund arises. The rider's case is confined to the phantom gantry line, and it succeeds on its own footing.

The platform's own routing confirms the gantry sits on no route it ever planned for this trip. The trip record's optimal route carries zero ERP (optimal_route_erp_sgd = 0.0), and the fare breakdown's money block books SGD 0.00 of ERP as on-optimal-route and the entire SGD 2.00 as off-optimal-route, with the gantry line itself flagged on_optimal_route = false. A gantry that is neither on the planned route nor anywhere near the driven trace has no basis to be billed to this rider at all.

The counterparty's entire answer is 'The ERP is charged by the system.' That assertion points to no artifact and no measurement, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion from either side that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. It cannot convert a trace whose nearest approach to the gantry is 4.85 km into a crossing, and it supplies no artifact that could corroborate the charge line.

This is not a case where a fare-breakdown line has baffled the record so that POL-RD-10(8) must send it to a human. POL-RD-09(4) expressly provides that POL-RD-10(8) is NOT triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb, and the policy's own commentary records the reason: a phantom line is both refundable and knowable, so the tribunal rules on it. The single unmatched line here is exactly that line, so the ruling should issue and the money should move.

The proximity measurement rests on a clean instrument. The GPS artifact is COMPLETE at a weight multiplier of 1.0: 107 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) are therefore not engaged, no straight-line-across-gap discount applies, and the 4,851.46 m nearest-approach figure can be taken at full weight under POL-GEN-02.

No traffic advisory is on file for this trip that could excuse any running outside the planned corridor. EV-ADVIS-03208-01 is MISSING - admissibility status MISSING, weight multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with the note that no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window. The rider cites that absence precisely because it is citable: with no advisory covering the trip window, the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and any external-traffic explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08 (POL-RD-13). Nothing in the bundle justifies a gantry charge the trace does not support. This claim relies on an artifact of weight 0.0 and does not ask it to carry any fact about the trip - only its own absence.

On quantum, the whole of the amount the rider contested comes back. The disputed line is SGD 2.00 and the correction under POL-RD-09(4) refunds it in full as a standalone item, comfortably above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and unaffected by the POL-RD-02 recomputation because no deviation is established. The rider's charge should not stand and the present state of the ledger should not be preserved under POL-GEN-03; the rider asks for the SGD 2.00 to be returned and a billing-integrity finding to be recorded in the ruling's referrals list - a referral, not an escalation, so the refund issues rather than being held.

The rider's route-deviation claim fails at the POL-RD-01 gate. The governing trace distance is 13.55 km against a booked optimal of 12.9 km: an excess of 0.65 km, or 5.04%, which is below both the 0.8 km absolute threshold and the 20% proportional threshold that POL-RD-01 requires to be passed together. No deviation is established on this trip, whatever the rider says about which roads were used.

POL-RD-01 requires the threshold test to be run on the trace figure, not the rounded copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km (13.55 km) governs over trip_record.actual_distance_km (13.6 km) where the two disagree, and the trip record figure may not be cited for the test. On the governing figure the excess is 0.65 km, and the platform's own derivation records the status as 'no deviation'.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged limb (b). The trip identifiers on TRP-03208 match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, but limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, and 0.65 km / 5.04% does not meet it. With no qualifying excess there is nothing for the driver to excuse, and a bare assertion that a road was 'never used' is not a measurement.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so no gap-handling treatment and no escalation discount applies: 107 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires, there is no POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger, and the deviation question is decidable on a clean, complete trace.

Because no deviation is established, the POL-RD-02 recomputation never runs and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider. POL-RD-09(1) confirms that off-route ERP is comprehended within a POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added on top of it; with no POL-RD-02 refund in existence there is no monetary ruling into which the $2.00 pass-through line could be folded as an add-on.

The billing-integrity limb of POL-RD-09(4) is not a computed finding on this record. The money block states in terms that the gantry match radius is a prose-only figure and that the ERP figures, which report the gantry coordinates, the $2.00 amount and the 4851 m nearest-fix distance, 'decide no match'. The limb therefore rests on the rider's proof, and the rider, who bears the burden of proof on this artifact set, has not put a match determination in evidence; the disputed line is in any event a system-levied pass-through, as the driver's on-file statement records.

No repeat-deviation pattern is engaged, so no POL-RD-06 consequence can attach: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 216, and neither limb of the pattern test (3 or more flags, or 5% or more with at least 40 completed trips) is met. There is therefore no balance resolved against the driver, no remedy uplift and no conduct referral; POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags for the trailing-90-day field the clause names.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver — this decision concerns the SGD 2.00 ERP line disputed on trip TRP-03208. It divides into two questions, and they come out differently.

1) Was there a route deviation? No. Measured on the governing trace figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 13.55 km (EV-GPS-03208), against the booked optimal of 12.9 km (EV-TRIP-03208), the excess is 0.65 km, or 5.04%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of the optimal; both tests fail, so no deviation exists and no POL-RD-02 distance-or-time refund is available. The trace is COMPLETE and unimpaired — 107 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 s — so POL-RD-07 imposes no gap discount and no corroboration requirement, and no POL-RD-10(3) trigger fires. The Driver's claims that no deviation is established, that the trace figure governs over trip_record.actual_distance_km, and that no repeat-deviation pattern applies (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 216, so POL-RD-06 gives no uplift and no conduct referral) are accepted.

2) Does the SGD 2.00 ERP line survive? No. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry's coordinates as a crossing. The gantry coordinates come from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-03208); the closest of the trace's 107 fixes lies 4,851.46 m from them, and no gap in the trace brackets a closest approach. The platform's own routing agrees: trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd = 0.0; the fare breakdown books SGD 0.00 of ERP as on-optimal-route and the entire SGD 2.00 as off-optimal-route; and the gantry line itself is flagged on_optimal_route = false. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes (or is never within 250 m of) is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refunded in full as a standalone correction, and that correction is available whether or not a deviation exists.

The Driver's answer — 'The ERP is charged by the system.' — points to no artifact and no measurement; under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight, and it cannot turn a nearest approach of 4.85 km into a crossing. The Driver's further contention that the gantry match 'decides no match' because the 250 m radius is a prose-only field is rejected: POL-RD-09 states that radius in terms and the geometry is already computed, so the match is run and it fails. For the same reasons the Driver's request for NO_ACTION is rejected — the present state should not be preserved for a line the trace does not support.

No escalation. POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged: POL-RD-09(4) states expressly that it is not triggered where the only unmatched fare line is one refunded under that limb, and the single unmatched line here is exactly that. No POL-RD-10(5) trigger fires: no party invoked a closure or other exculpatory clause against the absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-03208-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) — the advisory simply does not exist for this window, and the rider cites its absence only to note it, which under POL-RD-13 is not an escalation. POL-RD-09(1) is respected: off-route ERP is not added on top of any POL-RD-02 figure, because no POL-RD-02 refund exists; the SGD 2.00 moves as a standalone pass-through correction instead.

What moves. The contested amount is SGD 2.00 (the ERP line) and the refund is SGD 2.00, being the whole of it, so the outcome is FULL_REFUND. The monetary effect (SGD 2.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05) and executes automatically on issue. Every artifact this ruling rests on carries weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-03208, EV-FARE-03208), so no POL-GEN-02 discount applies. A billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) is recorded below; it rides with the refund and does not hold it.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' ERP line on TRP-03208 was charged for a gantry the GPS trace (EV-GPS-03208) never crosses — the closest of the 107 fixes lies 4,851.46 m from the gantry coordinates against the 250 m match radius — and is refunded in full as a standalone correction.
